title: Colossians
summary: Colossians is a biblical book focused on Christ's supremacy, union with Christ, new creation life, wisdom, and household witness.
historical_context: Colossians centers the church's identity and conduct in the supremacy and sufficiency of Christ.
ancient_near_east_context: Colossians belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Colossians should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Colossians as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Pauline Epistles, book 7 of 13, Colossians contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting Christ's supremacy, union with Christ, new creation life, wisdom, and household witness to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Colossians as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Colossians uses epistle within Pauline Epistles, book 7 of 13 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Colossians helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional Pauline authorship or Pauline circle attribution
Critical scholarship debates several letters and recognizes co-workers in some correspondence
date_ranges: Some disputed letters are placed later or in the Pauline school
original_audience: Mixed Jewish-Gentile congregations and church leaders across the Roman world
historical_setting: The Greco-Roman world of mission, patronage, and local house churches
canonical_role: Colossians anchors Christ's supremacy, union with Christ, new creation life, wisdom, and household witness within Pauline Epistles, book 7 of 13 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How doctrine, ethics, and pastoral counsel fit together

related_objects.notes: Paul frames the letter's teaching and prayer.
Christ's supremacy is the letter's theological center.
The letter describes renewed humanity in Christ.
Wisdom language shapes the letter's exhortation.
The church's identity is formed in Christ.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Colossians first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
The relationship links on Colossians are orientation anchors, not a full interpretive outline of the book.
